heroLine: Where Aman began, on its own peninsula above the Andaman Sea.
why: Place. Its own peninsula at Pansea Beach on Phuket's west coast, thirty minutes by car from Phuket International Airport.
Origin. Amanpuri opened in 1988 as the first property in the Aman portfolio, and it still presides over the same stretch of coast.
Privacy. Forty pool pavilions on the hillside and forty villas of three to nine bedrooms, each villa with its own pool, a Villa Host and a personal Thai chef.
signals: Its own peninsula at Pansea Beach, on Phuket's west coast.
Villas of three to nine bedrooms, each with its own pool.
A Villa Host and a personal Thai chef with every villa.
Thirty minutes by car from Phuket International Airport.
worth: Five nights. Two by the pool, one at sea in Phang Nga Bay or the Similans, and two with nowhere to be.
suits: Families and groups taking a villa
Children five and older, with the Eco-Beach Discovery Centre
Travellers pairing Phuket with Phang Nga Bay
notSuit: Travellers who want nightlife on the doorstep
Travellers looking for a remote outer island

heroLine: Four bedrooms, two pools and a 600 metre beach on Emerald Bay.
why: Place. Rosewood Phuket runs down a green hillside to its own 600 metre stretch of Emerald Bay, on Phuket's west coast.
Scale. The Palm House has four master bedrooms and two pools for up to twelve guests: a beach house for one family, with Rosewood behind it.
Care. A dedicated butler looks after the villas and houses, with Asaya, Rosewood's integrative wellness destination, a short walk away.
signals: A 600 metre beachfront on Emerald Bay.
Four master bedrooms and two pools, for up to twelve.
A dedicated butler in the villas and houses.
About 40 km from Phuket International Airport; Rosewood allows 60 to 90 minutes by road.
worth: Six nights. Long enough for the beach, Asaya and Ta Khai, and a day with nothing planned at all.
suits: Groups of friends of up to twelve
notSuit: Couples travelling alone (a pool villa suits better)
Travellers who want a short airport transfer

stayName: Four Seasons Tented Camp Golden Triangle
heroLine: Fifteen tents where Thailand, Myanmar and Laos meet.
why: Place. Bamboo jungle in Chiang Saen at the confluence of the Ruak and Mekong rivers, where Myanmar and Laos converge.
Elephants. My Elephant & I: walk with a herd and the camp's own mahouts through the grassland to the river.
Ease. Fifteen tents on decks over the Ruak and one two bedroom Explorer's Lodge, sold as all inclusive packages of two to four nights.
signals: At the confluence of the Ruak and Mekong, where three countries meet.
Sixteen places to stay in all: fifteen tents and one lodge.
The camp's own mahouts lead the walk with the elephants.
Chiang Rai International Airport (CEI) is the nearest airport.
A tented camp at the meeting of Thailand, Myanmar and Laos.
worth: Four nights. The four night package covers meals, drinks, spa and exploration, and the elephants deserve more than one morning.
suits: Couples (each tent takes up to three)
Families or small groups in the Explorer's Lodge, up to six
Travellers pairing the north with a beach in the south
notSuit: Travellers with only one night (packages start at two)
Travellers who want a pool with every room (only the Explorer's Lodge has one)

heroLine: One island, one resort, and its own airstrip.
why: Place. Pamalican, a small island in the Cuyo Archipelago ringed by white sand, with reefs that begin 300 metres offshore.
Access. Amanpulo's own twin turboprop flies from its lounge at Clark to the island's private airstrip in about 90 minutes.
Privacy. Forty three casitas and seventeen villas of one to four bedrooms, each villa with its own beach frontage, pool, private chef and butler.
signals: Pamalican, in the Cuyo Archipelago, with reefs from 300 metres offshore.
Seventeen villas, each with its own beach frontage and pool.
Amanpulo's own flights from Clark land on the island's airstrip in about 90 minutes.
A private chef and butler with every villa.
The only resort on Pamalican, where green and hawksbill turtles nest.
worth: Five nights. One for the reef, one for the kites or the turtles in season, and three for the island.
notSuit: Travellers who want to island hop by day

heroLine: A whole island off Palawan, for up to forty.
why: Place. A private island in a protected marine sanctuary off Palawan, inside the UNESCO Palawan Biosphere Reserve.
Privacy. Six beachfront villas, each with a pool of spring water from the island's own artesian well, and the island taken whole.
Humanity. Banwa works with its Aquos Foundation on turtle conservation and has recorded its 10,000th hawksbill nesting.
signals: A protected marine sanctuary in the UNESCO Palawan Biosphere Reserve.
Six beachfront villas and the whole island, for up to 40.
A direct helicopter transfer to the island.
The Aquos Foundation's hawksbill turtle work.
Tens of thousands of flying foxes leave Pagbu Island five minutes after sunset.
worth: Seven nights. Enough for the house reef, the flying foxes at Pagbu at sunset, and days that belong to nobody else.
notSuit: Travellers who want other guests and restaurants

heroLine: Seventeen tents in a national park on the Flores Sea.
why: Place. A beach-fringed bay on Moyo Island, inside Moyo Satonda National Park, looking over the Flores Sea to Medang Island and the mountains of Sumbawa.
Wild. Whale sharks in Saleh Bay with a guide from a local conservation group, untouched reefs to dive, and waterfalls in the jungle behind the camp.
Privacy. Seventeen tents and full board; book ten or more and the camp is yours.
signals: A bay inside Moyo Satonda National Park, on the Flores Sea.
Seventeen tents; ten or more make the camp your own.
Fly to Sumbawa Besar, then a 45 minute speedboat from Amanwana's own jetty.
Whale shark swims led by a local conservation guide.
A tented Aman inside a national park.
worth: Five nights. One for the whale sharks, two for the reefs, one for the waterfalls, and one to do nothing at all.
suits: Families or groups taking ten tents or more

heroLine: An island of its own, six lodges, in the Anambas.
why: Place. Elang is one of Bawah's six islands in Indonesia's remote Anambas archipelago, with two beaches kept for Elang guests alone.
Privacy. Six standalone cliffside lodges, five of one bedroom and one of two, with a club house, an owner's lounge, a saltwater infinity pool and the Beach House restaurant, bought out whole.
Care. A personal butler in every lodge, the Kayu Spa, and Bawah's all inclusive days: meals, a spa treatment each night, yoga and the lagoons.
signals: One of six islands in the Anambas, with two private beaches.
Six lodges for one party of up to 14.
An 80 minute seaplane from Batam that lands in the lagoon.
A personal butler in every lodge.
A private island inside a private island reserve.
worth: Five nights. Bawah's minimum is three; the lagoons, the reefs and Elang's own beaches need five.
suits: Families with children five and older
Groups of friends of up to 14
notSuit: Families with children under five (Bawah welcomes five and older)
Travellers who pack heavy (the seaplane allows 15 kg each)
